title: Check if DFS Strings Are Palindromes
summary: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a character from a string s, perform a depth-first search (DFS) to construct a string dfsStr for each node.
statement: Given a tree with nodes numbered from 0 to n-1, where each node has a character from a string s, perform a depth-first search (DFS) to construct a string dfsStr for each node. For each node, clear dfsStr, perform DFS starting from that node, and check if the resulting string is a palindrome. Return an array indicating whether each node's DFS string is a palindrome.
constraints: parent and s describe a rooted tree of up to 100,000 nodes; parent[0] is -1.
A node’s DFS word visits children in increasing node order and appends the node character after all children.
Return whether every node’s complete subtree DFS word is a palindrome.
hints: Every subtree occupies one contiguous interval in the global postorder character sequence.
Build that sequence and each interval, then preprocess all odd/even palindrome radii with Manacher’s algorithm.
Iterative postorder records subtree size and end; query the appropriate center radius for each interval.
Postorder contiguity converts every subtree question to an exact substring query, and Manacher answers all such queries in linear total time.
editorial: Postorder contiguity converts every subtree question to an exact substring query, and Manacher answers all such queries in linear total time.
